title: ops seller skill bridge microdeck (wip)
content:
Purpose:
Short microdeck to upskill field sellers (ops-focused SEs and AMs) to run low-friction pilot conversations with platform and infra teams. Focus: fallback economics, canary scripts, operational checklist, sample talk tracks. This is NOT a full sales deck — it is a set of compact slides + speaker notes for a 10–12 minute technical seller demo + Q&A.

Audience:
- Platform engineers, infra leads, SREs evaluating inference integration
- Sellers/SEs who need quick ops-focused rebuttals and a fast pilot checklist

TL;DR (slide 1):
- What we want them to do: run a 2-week low-risk pilot that proves latency, stability and cost per RU
- Seller asks: get 2 metrics (p95 latency end-to-end, cost per 1k tokens) and one qualitative signal (error modes)
- Fallback posture: graceful degrade to cheaper model variant + region fallback

Slide 2 — Quick opener (30s)
- 1-line problem: unpredictable inference unit economics + noisy tail latencies during peak traffic
- Our claim: Redwood reduces tail risk with batching + routing and makes fallback deterministic
- Proof hook: show one-line benchmark (example numbers)

Speaker note: keep it concrete — call out a specific customer problem (e.g., autofill pipeline that spiked week-over-week). Ask the prospect: what do you measure during incidents?

Slide 3 — The pilot play (2 slides condensed)
- Duration: 2 weeks (rolling canary for 48h then full ramp)
- Inputs: sample traffic dump (1–2 hours), target SLOs (p95 latency < 250ms for critical route), token budget cap
- Outputs: p95/p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, error types and frequency

Checklist (seller script bullets):
- Pre-call: request 1-hour traffic extract and current model config
- Day 0: onboarding — connect via Private or Dedicated staging, deploy canary routing rule
- Day 2–3: validate telemetry and trace tags (trace-id parity)
- Day 7: operational review; agree to roll or rollback

Slide 4 — Fallback matrix (battlecard style)
- Failure mode: spike in latency
  - Root cause quick triage: per-host CPU vs queue depth vs KV cache miss
  - Immediate mitigation: switch to model-variant-quantized or route to dedicated pool
  - Customer-facing message: "We’ve moved your non-critical routes to quantized variant to stabilize latency while preserving core quality"
- Failure mode: cost overshoot
  - Mitigation: enable prefix-caching and token cap; schedule model quota throttles
  - Message: "Temporary cost cap applied; ops will post-mortem patterns and recommend batching rules"

Slide 5 — Live demo script (3–4 minutes)
- Show routing policy UI: create rule that routes {100% traffic of route X} to canary model for 48h
- Toggle fallback: flip to quantized variant and show latency change in realtime (demo telemetry)
- Show console trace: sample request -> model selection -> response time breakdown (tokenization, model compute, network)

Speaker note: have screenshots ready; if demo instability, switch to annotated screenshots. Emphasize time-to-rollback (~minutes)

Slide 6 — Ops-ready battlecard one-pager (what seller tucks in pocket)
- Quick metrics to gather pre-call: route name, p50/p95/p99, average tokens per request, daily request volume
- One-liner responses to common ops objections:
  - "We can’t change model versions mid-pilot" -> "We use canary routing and read-only query duplication; rollback is a single toggle"
  - "Latency variability is due to our upstream DB" -> "We instrument trace-id parity and can isolate model-side delay; we’ll add route-level sampling"
  - "We need SOC controls" -> "Private deployment option, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs — can be scoped to pilot"

Slide 7 — Success criteria & acceptance rubric
- Pass if: p95 within 1.2x of baseline and cost delta < 20% OR measurable reduction in error spikes
- Partial pass: shows improvement in either latency or cost and clear path for remaining issue (e.g., cache tuning)
- Fail: no measurable improvement and repeated unresolvable model-side errors

Slide 8 — Quick technical appendix (for SEs)
- What we tweak during pilot: batch window (ms), max batch size, KV cache TTL, quantization flag, routing weights
- Telemetry to check: per-host queue depth, GPU utilization, tokenization time, micro-burst rate

Slide 9 — Mini postmortem template (seller leaves this behind)
- Summary: high-level outcome, dates
- Metrics collected (attach dashboard link)
- Actions taken during pilot (rollbacks, fallback triggers)
- Recommended next steps (dedicated reservation, extended pilot, or private deployment)

Appendix — Quick rebut playbook (copyable snippets)
- Rebut: "We don’t want vendor lock-in" -> "APIs are consistent; you can pin model versions and export configs; migration plan template included"
- Rebut: "We only trust in-house infra" -> "Private deployment + on-prem package keeps control and audit logs under your team"

Open issues / TODOs (internal):
- Add real anonymized benchmark screenshots for 3 example verticals (FinServ, eComm, Support) — @Connor
- Build a 60s GIF of toggling fallback and latency graph — @Miguel
- Fast-check legal once pilot data retention >90 days — @Priya

Action items after call:
- Share pilot checklist + minimal telemetry spec
- Create Jira ticket GTO-PILOT-<account> for ops runbook and assign SE

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep language ops-friendly, avoid marketing-speak ("economics" -> "cost per 1k tokens")
- Practice the 3-line opener: problem, claim, proof hook
- This microdeck should be printable as a one-pager for quick in-person handoff

End.
